summary: This wiki-sourced article describes Miami, Florida, covering its role as a television, music and film production hub for Spanish-language media, its professional sports teams and events, and its economy and tourism. It also covers the city's history, Cleanest City and poverty rankings, neighborhoods, the Miami accent, PortMiami and Miami International Airport, climate, and city government.
one_line: Overview of Miami, Florida: its media and music industries, sports, economy, port and airport, history, climate, neighborhoods and government.
key_facts: Univisión, Telemundo and UniMÁS have their headquarters in Miami, and Miami is the most important U.S. city for Spanish-language media.
In 2011, 85% of Telemundo's original programming was filmed in Miami.
Miami's four major professional teams are the Miami Dolphins, Miami Heat, Miami Marlins and Florida Panthers.
Forbes magazine ranked Miami "America's Cleanest City" in 2008.
In a 2009 UBS study of 73 world cities, Miami was ranked the richest city in the United States and the world's fifth-richest city in terms of purchasing power.
In 2004, Miami had the third highest incidence of family incomes below the federal poverty line in the United States.
Miami's local government went bankrupt in 2001.
Julia Tuttle, a local citrus grower and wealthy Cleveland native, is noted as the only major U.S. city conceived by a woman.
Miami was officially incorporated as a city on July 28, 1896, with a population of just over 300.
The Great Freeze of 1894–95 hastened Miami's growth because its crops were the only ones in Florida that survived.
PortMiami is called the "Cruise Capital of the World" and served 3,787,410 passengers in 2007.
Miami International Airport caters to over 35 million passengers a year and is the single largest international gateway for American Airlines.
Tourism draws over 38 million visitors annually, spending $17.1 billion.
Miami has a tropical monsoon climate (Köppen Am), with January averaging 67.2 °F (19.6 °C).
The 2010 Census-based metropolitan population exceeded 5.5 million, making Miami's metro area the largest in the Southeastern United States.
